messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Onyx Health (enterprise) - eu-west dedicated cluster degraded. Paging on-call now. Impact: increased tail latency, intermittent webhook delivery failures to customer contact endpoints. Start triage thread here.

Maya (oncall): I’m on it. Can someone paste the alert details?

incident-bot: Alert:
- name: dedicated-pool-eu-west-high-queue
- severity: P1
- triggered: 2355559875
- symptom: request_queue_size > 200 for 5m on pool: onyx-eu-west-dedicated
- automated actions: rate-limit disabled, autoscaler did not spin additional nodes (maxed).

Jeremy (SRE): Seeing sustained replica CPU at ~98% and worker goroutines stuck on `kv-cache` locks. Also multiple 502s logged from the webhook dispatcher to https://hooks.onyx-health.com/ping. Logs: 
```
2026-03-15T10:01:12Z dispatcher.go:214 error="post https://hooks.onyx-health.com/ping: dial tcp 10.20.34.5:443: connect: connection timed out"
2026-03-15T10:02:03Z runtime/serve.go:678 warn="kv cache miss storm, eviction thrash"
```

Maya (oncall): Lia, can you confirm customer-visible symptoms? Are they seeing errors in their app or just latency?

Lia (Customer Success): Onyx reports failed webhook deliveries for retryable events (billing.notify, contact-routing). Primary platform UX shows long LLM response times for heavy inference routes. Their SOC flagged it and asked for an ETA. I told them we’re investigating; they want an incident timeline and a tailored impact blurb for their stakeholders.

Patrick (Eng - Runtime): Quick mitigation path: 1) shift Onyx traffic from `onyx-eu-west-dedicated` to `hosted-eu` (compatible model v2.1) via routing policy fallback; 2) restart a subset of affected runtime nodes to clear KV-cache thrash; 3) temporarily enable aggressive prefix caching on Onyx prefix to reduce inference load. Can do steps 1+2 in ~8-12m.

Maya (oncall): Jeremy, please coordinate the node restarts. I’ll prepare routing fallback and customer comm drafts. Who owns the routing policy change?

Jeremy (SRE): I’ll do the restarts. Ops Rotation — can you approve scheduled rolling restart (non-destructive, 1 node at a time)? :thumbsup:

Ops Rotation: Approved. Keep canary size = 1, soak 2m between restarts.

Patrick (Eng - Runtime): Routing change command (run from ops-console):
```
redwood route update --customer onyx --from onyx-eu-west-dedicated --to hosted-eu --policy fallback --dry-run=false
```
I’ll gate the command on the restart beginning.

Maya (oncall): Lia, draft for Onyx stakeholders (short, tailored):
> Short impact: "We are experiencing degraded performance and intermittent webhook delivery failures for your eu-west dedicated deployment. Some automated event deliveries may have been delayed or retried. Our mitigation includes temporarily routing traffic to hosted eu capacity and restarting a subset of nodes to restore normal throughput."

Lia (Customer Success): That reads well. Add ETA: "We expect restoration of normal service for most traffic within 30 minutes after the routing change." Also include recommended action: "If you see duplicate webhook deliveries, please pause automated downstream processing for 15 minutes and reach out to your CSM."

Maya (oncall): Draft status page update (short form):
> Status: Degraded performance (eu-west dedicated pool)
> Affected: Onyx Health (dedicated pool: onyx-eu-west), potential downstream webhook failures for some customers.
> Timeline: Investigating — mitigation in progress (routing to hosted-eu + node restarts). Next update in 15 minutes.

Patrick (Eng - Runtime): Sending routing change now. Executing: `redwood route update --customer onyx --from onyx-eu-west-dedicated --to hosted-eu --policy fallback`

incident-bot: Route update job queued: job_id=job_89234. Will post when complete.

Jeremy (SRE): Beginning rolling restart of the runtime pool. Restarting node onyx-eu-west-03 now. Logs show eviction pressure decreasing after restart.

Maya (oncall): Status: routing job completed; job_89234 -> success. Onyx traffic now moving to hosted-eu with graceful drain.

Jeremy (SRE): Node restarts: 03 -> success, 04 -> success, 02 -> success. Eviction thrash reduced, queue size trending down from 230 -> 40 over 10 minutes. Webhook dispatcher retries succeeding (200s).

Lia (Customer Success): Onyx CSM update (send now):
```
Hi Onyx team — quick update: We've routed your traffic to additional hosted capacity and restarted affected nodes. Most webhook retries are now completing successfully. We expect normal operation for most requests within 30 minutes. If you continue to see errors, please escalate to your CSM or reply here. — Lia
```

Maya (oncall): Good. I’ll post to internal #status-updates and update the public status page with the draft.

Maya (oncall): Internal comms template for enterprise ops (for legal/CS/AM):
- Incident ID: INC-2026-0315-onyx-eu
- Scope: Onyx Health dedicated eu-west pool (onyx-eu-west-dedicated)
- Customer impact: degraded inference latency (10-90s), intermittent webhook delivery failures for automated event endpoints. Potential duplicate deliveries due to retries.
- Mitigation: temporary routing to hosted-eu, rolling restart of 3 nodes, enabled aggressive prefix caching.
- Current status: mitigation complete, monitoring. Queue sizes stabilized.
- Next steps: keep monitoring for 2 hours, revert routing after capacity stable or schedule planned re-provisioning of dedicated pool.

Patrick (Eng - Runtime): Note for backend: schedule a follow-up to bump autoscaler max for this dedicated pool and run a postmortem on kv-cache contention and routing policy thresholds.

Maya (oncall): Handoff plan: I’m handing to Jeremy for post-incident monitoring and follow-up actions (PM, postmortem, autoscaler bump). Jeremy — you own the incident now.

Jeremy (SRE): Taking over. I’ll open INC ticket, assign postmortem owner, capture metrics. Lia — please send the customer follow-up email with the final impact blurb and incident reference.

Lia (Customer Success): Will do. Draft email (final):
```
Subject: Incident INC-2026-0315-onyx-eu — Temporary degraded performance and webhook retries

Hello Onyx team,

We experienced degraded performance in your eu-west dedicated environment which caused intermittent webhook delivery failures and increased inference latency. We have temporarily routed traffic to hosted eu capacity and restarted the affected nodes. Most traffic is restored; we estimate full stability within 30 minutes. We will follow up with a post-incident report including root cause and mitigation details.

If you observe duplicate events, please hold downstream processing for ~15 minutes and notify your CSM.

Apologies for the disruption — Lia
```

Maya (oncall): Closing notes: incident severity to be reviewed by execs; recommend P1->P2 after confirmation of stability. Add action item: telemetry alert tuning for `kv-cache` thrash and a new test to validate webhook dispatcher backoff behavior.

incident-bot: Incident HANDOFF recorded: owner=Jeremy, state=monitoring, incident_id=INC-2026-0315-onyx-eu.

Jeremy (SRE): I’ll run a 2-hour watch and pull logs for a postmortem. Assigning postmortem to Patrick.

Patrick (Eng - Runtime): Accepted, will own follow-up. I’ll coordinate with infra to raise autoscaler limits and add stronger eviction instrumentation.

Lia (Customer Success): Onyx confirmed receipt and appreciates proactive updates. They asked for the postmortem when available.

Maya (oncall): Thanks team. Ending active paging — moving to watch. :white_check_mark:
